comment: The security principle addresses protection of the infrastructure but not the systemic risk that shared infrastructure creates. public.text: The security principle addresses protection of the infrastructure but not the systemic risk that shared infrastructure creates. Consolidating on one normative authority, one certification gate and a smaller set of conformant products reduces diversity, and reduced diversity means correlated vulnerability: one flaw in the certified implementation is a flaw across the system. Fragmented landscapes have the underappreciated property of failing in small pieces.
public.suggestedRevision: State the trade-off explicitly with its design consequences: do not mandate a single reference implementation, since that makes monoculture a requirement rather than an outcome; require degraded operating modes that keep care possible during outage, and require that they be exercised rather than only documented; and place national testing and validation capability under the same continuity regime as the components it certifies, so the conformance gate is not itself a single point of failure.
